newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end up on cash bond buying, short-squeezing.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end up on cash bond buying, short-squeezing.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply higher on Friday due to cash bond buying by investors and short-squeezing by dealers.
The March's surge was fueled by demand for cash bonds by investors, a trader for a city bank's securities affiliate said.
Various investors, including banks, were detected buying long-term cash JGBs and some were detected selling put options, the trader said.
Agricultural financial institutions were detected buying the new 35th 20-year JGBs, a brokerage house trader said.
A trader at a regional bank said there was talk that agricultural financial institutions had bought 10-year JGBs between the 180th to the 189th issues.
The release of Bank of Japan's quarterly economic report late in afternoon trade on Friday had little effect on JGBs, the first trader said.

The BOJ said in the report that it would closely watch the effect of recent falls in Japanese stock prices on corporate sentiment. Also, it stuck to its recent assessment that the economy was recovering gradually and private demand gradually becoming more firm.
The March ended at 126.22, up sharply from Thursday's 125.66. Turnover was 54,609 contracts.

The BOJ's announcement on Thursday that it would release its key quarterly "tankan" survey in early April instead of late February triggered speculation that Japanese corporate earnings results might be much worse than expected, and led to buying of JGBs, traders said.
A fall in Tokyo share prices during the day was also a buy factor for JGBs, the first trader said.
In the Tokyo stock market, the 225-share Nikkei average ended down 220.10 points, at 17,689.36.
A 10-year JGB auction is likely to take place on Tuesday, the first trader said.

Although the coupon rate for these new issues was likely to be set at an all-time low of 2.6 percent, judging from current market levels, there probably would be demand for the bonds from investors, the trader said.
The trader said there was strong demand for the recently auctioned 20-year issues, even with a record-low coupon rate of 3.3 percent, indicating there was demand for new JGB issues.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.410 percent as of 0706 GMT, down from 2.425 percent on Thursday.
